Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh rate and matched frame cap provide a smooth, stable experience that suits the slow-paced city-building gameplay; upscaling from 1024x640 keeps the image sharp enough at Deck screen size. This profile holds well in mid-sized cities but expect dips in very large, heavily trafficked cities due to CPU simulation limits.

profiles.Summary: Cities: Skylines runs on the Steam Deck under Proton (gold tier) and is playable, though larger cities with high populations can cause significant CPU-driven frame drops due to the game's single-threaded simulation workload. Medium settings at native resolution are generally achievable in early-game, but late-game sprawl may require dialing back to low settings and a 30 fps cap to stay stable.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC requirements (the Deck's GPU is roughly GTX 1050 Ti class, comfortably above the minimum but below recommended) and the known CPU-bound nature of Cities: Skylines' simulation. On your first session, monitor frame rate as your city grows — large cities will CPU-bottleneck before the GPU does, so switch to a lower profile if frame rates drop in busy areas.

MaxBattery.Notes: Downscaling to 960x600 with FSR significantly reduces GPU load, leaving more headroom for the CPU simulation; battery life gains are most pronounced in early-game small cities. In large late-game cities, the 30 fps cap may still be broken by CPU bottlenecks regardless of GPU settings.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native resolution with high settings is achievable in early and mid-game where the city is small, but the 60 fps cap will not be sustained in large cities due to the single-threaded CPU simulation bottleneck. If frame rates drop below 40 fps in late-game, consider switching to the Optimal profile.

Optimal.Notes: Locking to 40 fps at 40 Hz gives the smoothest pacing for a strategy/simulation title where constant mouse interaction matters more than raw frame rate. FSR upscaling from 1024x640 keeps the city readable while saving GPU headroom for the CPU to breathe.
